quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When going through a curve, you should:

options.text: Stay in the same part of the lane the whole time.
Stay in the left part of the lane the whole time.
Stay in the right part of the lane the whole time.
Know that the best path may not follow the curve of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know that the best path may not follow the curve of the road.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change. Be ready to change your lane position when needed. The best path through a curve may not follow the road's curve.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.explanation: To ride safely on a slippery surface, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes if you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: A helmeted rider is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should be placed:

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: A motorcycle passenger:

options.text: Must wear a helmet if under 18 years old.
Must wear a helmet if they don't have a motorcycle license.
Must wear a helmet if the operator's license is less than two years old.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must wear a helmet if under 18 years old.
questions.explanation: In Hawaii, any motorcycle operator or passenger under 18 must wear an approved helmet. All operators and passengers should wear helmets for safety.

questions.question: If you lock your rear wheel while braking on a good road surface, you should:

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and quickly reapply it.
Release the rear brake and downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear brake locks on a good road surface, keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it stays upright and straight.

questions.question: When braking in a curve:

options.text: It works the same as braking on a straight road.
You have more grip as you lean into the curve.
You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. Your tires are already using grip to turn, so less grip is available for braking.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell riders about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of your lane should you use?

options.text: The left part of the lane
The middle part of the lane
The right part of the lane
Either the left or right part of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left part of the lane
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, ride in the left part of your lane. This keeps you away from opening car doors, people stepping between cars, and cars pulling out.

questions.question: Motorcycle headlights are:

options.text: Usually more powerful than car headlights.
Usually just as powerful as car headlights.
Usually less powerful than car headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually less powerful than car headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: When riding with a heavy load, you should adjust the:
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to the settings recommended for the added weight.

questions.question: When following a car, ride in which portion of the lane?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Most drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips under five miles long at speeds slower than 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: A helmet should not:

options.text: Have been worn in an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have been worn in an accident.
questions.explanation: A good helmet meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly, and has no obvious defects. Replace any helmet that was worn during a crash.

questions.question: Proper riding clothing provides all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Proper riding clothing protects you from injury in a collision and from weather hazards. It increases your comfort, not discomfort.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: At the end of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them without making inexperienced riders lead the group.

questions.question: When entering a turn, a rider should:

options.text: Move their shoulders to match the turn angle.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down by releasing the throttle and applying both brakes if needed.

questions.question: The center of the lane often has an oily strip. You should:

options.text: Avoid it when roads are wet.
Ride only on it for better traction.
Avoid the entire center of the lane.
Not worry about oil in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid it when roads are wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars builds up in the center of lanes. On dry roads, it usually provides enough traction. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride around it while staying in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: If you lock the rear tire on a surface with good traction, you should:

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you stop.
Release the brake and use only the front brake.
Release the brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear brake on a good surface, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can still steer your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handlebar grip opposite to the direction you want to turn.
Do not hold the grip because it is dangerous.
Do not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When going faster than walking speed, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the grip in the direction you want to turn. This will make you lean the right way.

questions.question: How do you stop quickly on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use the rear brake hard while slowly increasing the front brake pressure.

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: To ride safely on slippery surfaces, use both brakes when slowing or stopping, slow down, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oil, dirt, gravel, shaded areas, and bridges—these are more slippery than other surfaces.

questions.question: For an eye or face shield to work well, it must:

options.text: Block all air from passing through.
Not allow eyeglasses to fit underneath.

questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must have no scratches, resist damage, allow clear side views, fasten securely, allow air to pass through to prevent fogging, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: When entering a highway or curve, how should a group of motorcyclists ride?

options.text: Ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best, but switch to single-file when turning, going through curves, or entering or leaving a highway.
